agent.problem: The opening card already says that the crowd is standing between Zacchaeus and his view of Jesus. This supplies the real reason he cannot see and rules out card 2's claim that Jesus has already gone by, giving away the later true-or-false answer.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

agent.problem: Cards 10 and 11 ask about the crowd's reaction before any story card sets up that reaction. Card 10 introduces the people seeing Jesus go with Zacchaeus only inside its own true-or-false statement, and card 11 introduces their grumbling inside its own question. The grumbling is not told on a story card until card 12, afterward, so the setup was not already told when these consecutive choice cards appeared.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is on a story card. Not every choice card needs its own story card right before it: a choice card can follow another choice card when the setup is already told.

human.problem: Card 19 introduces "the Son of Man" without saying who He is. The text doesn't state here that Jesus is speaking of Himself.
human.question: Should Papa Dorin say simply who the Son of Man is (Jesus, speaking of Himself), as the new-people rule asks? Or should he leave it open because Luke 19:10 doesn't say it, and let a dictionary pop-up cover it?
